cards.text: A father is giving his son some serious advice, and friend, this is NOT a suggestion box. He opens with: "My son, keep my words and treasure my commandments within you."

cards.question: The father tells his son that keeping his commandments leads to life.

cards.text: He tells his son to guard his teachings as the apple of his eye, tie them to his fingers, and write them on the tablet of his heart. Fingers AND heart, friend, this dad is covering EVERY base.

cards.question: Why would the father want his teachings tied to his son's fingers and written on his heart?

answers.text: So they stay close all the time
So others can read them aloud
So he can recite them at the gate

cards.text: Then he tells his son to say to wisdom, "You are my sister," and to call understanding his kinsman. Wisdom's not some coworker you nod at in the elevator, friend, she's FAMILY.

cards.question: Wisdom and understanding will keep the son from the ___, the stranger with seductive words.

cards.text: Then the father tells what he saw, and every street's got one of these: the neighbor at the window who sees EVERYTHING. He says, "For at the window of my house I looked through the lattice."

cards.question: Watching through the lattice, the father notices among the simple youths a young man lacking ___.

cards.text: This young man is crossing the street near her corner, strolling down the road to her house. Not lost, not running late, friend, he's STROLLING.

cards.question: When is the young man strolling down the road to her house?

answers.text: At twilight as day fades to dark
At sunrise as the city wakes up
At noon in the heat of the day

cards.text: Then a woman comes out to meet him. She's wearing the attire of a harlot, and she's cunning of heart.

cards.question: The father describes this woman as quiet and happy to stay at home.

cards.text: She's loud and defiant, and she's in the street, in the squares, lurking at every corner. She's everywhere, friend, like crumbs after I bake a batch.

cards.question: The woman walks right up to the young man. What does she do?

answers.text: She seizes him and kisses him

cards.text: Then she starts talking. She tells him she's made her peace offerings and paid her vows today, and I bet she's had that opening line ready for a WHILE.

cards.question: The woman tells the young man she sought him and found him.

cards.text: Then she tells him she's decked her bed with colored linen from Egypt and perfumed it with myrrh, aloes and cinnamon. She's not hoping he shows up, friend, she's got the place READY.

cards.question: Fancy linens and perfume all ready to go. What does the woman invite the young man to do?

answers.text: Take their fill of love till morning
Help her pay her vows at the temple
Rest a while and then head home

cards.text: Then she brings up her husband. Friend, when the pitch comes with a husband update, that's your cue to LEAVE.

cards.question: The woman tells the young man her husband is at home tonight.

cards.text: He's gone on a long journey, she says, with a bag of money, and he won't be back till the moon is full. That's not an invitation anymore, friend, that's a TRAVEL itinerary.

cards.question: The woman gets the young man to go along with her through great persuasion and flattering ___.

cards.text: He follows her on impulse, like an ox going to the slaughter, like a deer bounding into a trap. That's the father's picture, and whew, it is NOT a flattering one.

cards.question: An ox headed to the slaughter and a deer bounding into a trap. What do those pictures say about the young man?

answers.text: He's being chased by a hunter
He's strong enough to break free

cards.text: The father finishes it: an arrow pierces his liver, like a bird darting into a snare, not knowing it will cost him his life. All that, friend, from a stroll down the wrong street.
Now the father turns to his sons and tells them to listen to him and attend to the words of his mouth. Friend, this is the part of the meeting where NOBODY checks their email.

cards.question: What does the father tell his sons about the woman's ways?

answers.text: Don't let their hearts turn aside to them
Go once and see them for themselves
Warn her husband when he gets back

cards.question: The father says the woman has brought only a few people down.

cards.text: Many, friend. Her slain are many in number, and the father has one last line about where her house really leads.

cards.question: The father says her house is the road to ___, descending to the chambers of death.

findings.problem: The question asks why the father wants his teachings tied to the son's fingers and written on his heart, and the right answer gives a reason the text never states (so they stay close all the time). The only purpose the passage gives is in 7:5, that wisdom and understanding may keep the son from the adulteress. The card presents an interpretation as the father's stated reason.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question says wisdom and understanding 'will keep' the son from the adulteress. The BSB says 'that they may keep you,' which is a purpose, not a promise. The card turns the text into a guarantee.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: In 7:22-23, 'until an arrow pierces his liver' belongs to the chain of comparisons (like an ox, like a deer, like a bird). The card pulls it out as a plain statement, 'an arrow pierces his liver,' so it reads as something that literally happens to the young man. The text keeps it inside the comparison.

The right answer, 'Don't let their hearts turn aside to them,' is the only answer in Bible phrasing. The wrong answers ('Go once and see them for themselves', 'Warn her husband when he gets back') sound casual and modern, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
